name: Blackletter
summary: The broken letter of the Gothic book hand: narrow, dark, with strokes that turn at sharp angles instead of curves. Gutenberg printed his Bible in textura; Fraktur stayed the German text face until 1941. Today it carries tradition, heraldry, metal and rebellion.

philosophy.core_thesis: A letter written with a broad nib held at a steep angle breaks each curve into straight strokes and makes a dark, even texture on the page.
design_principles: Break the round strokes into straight segments that meet at angles; the bowl of the o is a hexagon or a lozenge in textura.
Hold the nib at 30–45°, so the vertical stems are heavy and the diagonals and joins are hairlines.
Keep the letters narrow and the space inside them about equal to the stem, so the line is a dark, even band.
Give the stems diamond feet and heads (textura) or a forked or curved top (Fraktur).
Make the capitals rich and round, with spurs and hairline flourishes, and never set a full word in them.
Use the long s (ſ) and the ligatures ch, ck, tz and ſt in Fraktur text.
anti_patterns: Wide letter spacing or positive tracking
Smooth round bowls as in a roman
A blackletter for long text on a screen for a general reader
Blackletter mixed with a script in one line

classification.note: DIN 16518 has five sub-groups: Gotisch (textura), Rundgotisch (rotunda), Schwabacher, Fraktur and Fraktur-Varianten. Vox (1954) put blackletter in the graphic class; ATypI added the class when it adopted the scheme in 1962.

anatomy.contrast: Clear: the stems are heavy, and the diagonals and joins are hairlines of 0.1–0.3 of the stem.
anatomy.stress: Diagonal, from a nib held at 30–45°; the curves are broken into straight strokes.
anatomy.serifs: No true serifs: diamond-shaped feet and heads in textura, forked or split tops in Fraktur.
anatomy.terminals: Sharp, angled cuts and small hairline spurs at the ends of the strokes.
anatomy.aperture: Closed: the c, e and a are narrow and dark.
anatomy.key_letters: A long s (ſ), an a with a closed, angular bowl, an o made of straight strokes, and round, decorated capitals.

metrics.x_height: The x-height is 0.66–0.82 of the cap height; the ascenders are short and the capitals are tall and broad.
metrics.contrast: The o test gives 1.0–2.0: with a broad nib at angle θ, the side of the o is nib·cos θ wide and the top is nib·sin θ thick, so the ratio is cot θ, 1.73 at 30° and 1.0 at 45°. The real contrast is between the stems and the hairline diagonals.
metrics.width: Narrow: the mean advance of a to z is 0.38–0.45 em.
metrics.figures: Lining figures, drawn with the same broken strokes.

setting.text_sizes: For text, set Fraktur at 11–14 pt or 18–22 px, and only for readers who know it.
setting.display_sizes: Set titles, mastheads and labels at 24–120 pt.
setting.leading: Set the leading at 1.2–1.35 for text and 1.0–1.1 for titles.
setting.tracking: Set 0 em; for emphasis, Fraktur uses letter spacing (Sperrsatz) of about 0.15 em on one word, not bold.
setting.measure: Set 40–60 characters a line; the narrow letters give more words a line than a roman.
setting.case_and_features: Use upper and lower case only, and turn on the ligatures and the long s if the font has them.

pairing.rule: Use blackletter for one masthead or title and set all running text in a calm roman or a plain sans.

pairs.why: The roman grew out of a rejection of the Gothic hand, so the two give a clear historical contrast.
The plain grotesque does not compete with the texture of the broken letter.

reference_faces.note: UnifrakturMaguntia is a free Fraktur from a 1901 model. Pirata One and Grenze Gotisch are new display faces of the class, not revivals of one cut.

evidence.title: Gutenberg Bible (B42), the opening of Genesis
evidence.credit: Gutenberg Bible page; scan on Wikimedia Commons

emotion.target_response: Weight and tradition: the reader feels age, ritual and authority, or rebellion when the context is music or street culture.

avoid_when: The text is longer than a title and the readers are not used to Fraktur.
The brand must look neutral or modern.

modifiers.how: Use a roman with the same dark colour and a diagonal stress; keep blackletter only for the initial.
Keep the narrow, dark band, but drop the broken strokes for a condensed bold grotesque.

stroke_contrast.note: The o test misleads here; the value is the stem against the hairline.

tracking.note: Sperrsatz spaces one word by about 0.15 em for emphasis.

sources.title: Robert Bringhurst, The Elements of Typographic Style (Hartley & Marks, 4th ed. 2012)
